sources.entry: Tube Archivist ⚠ - Organize, search, and enjoy your YouTube collection. Subscribe, download, and track viewed content with metadata indexing and a user-friendly interface. (Source Code, Clients) GPL-3.0 Docker
Tube Archivist | Archive and index your favourite YouTube channels

summary.one_liner: Tube Archivist is a self-hosted, Docker-based web app that downloads, indexes, and organizes your YouTube channel subscriptions and videos for offline search and playback.
summary.what_it_does: It lets you subscribe to YouTube channels and download videos using yt-dlp, then indexes them with metadata from YouTube so they can be searched and browsed through a web interface. It tracks which videos have been viewed or not viewed. The README also mentions playlists, SponsorBlock integration, subtitle download and indexing, comment download, per-channel settings, and scheduled rescans and downloads. Authentication options include local accounts, LDAP, and reverse-proxy forwarded auth. Elasticsearch is used for search and Redis is a required connection.
use_cases: archive a YouTube channel for offline viewing
search a large downloaded YouTube video collection
track watched and unwatched YouTube videos
subscribe to channels and auto-download new uploads
self-hosted YouTube media server for kids or family
feed archived videos into Jellyfin or Plex
how_to_run: Install Docker and make sure it is running.
Copy the example docker-compose.yml from the repository.
Set the required environment variables: TA_HOST, TA_USERNAME, TA_PASSWORD, ELASTIC_PASSWORD, REDIS_CON, and TZ.
On Linux hosts, set vm.max_map_count to at least 262144 for Elasticsearch.
Start the stack with docker compose and open the web interface.
In settings, set the download format, subscribe to channels, then start the download.
notable: Browser companion extension for Firefox and Chrome, plus Jellyfin and Plex plugins
Per-channel settings and optional auto-deletion of watched items
Backup and restore, and import from JSON files
Optional automatic yt-dlp updates on container start
caveats: Needs about 2GB RAM for a small setup and about 4GB for mid to large installations, plus Elasticsearch.
Inherits all yt-dlp limitations; videos YouTube or yt-dlp cannot extract will not download.
Media file naming is not flexible, and created files must be playable in the browser you use.
